title: Capture taken on a host using segmentation offload (TSO/GSO/LRO)
summary: 8 TCP segments are larger than the negotiated MSS and 4 IPv4 packets have total length 0. The network card splits or merges these on the wire, so the capture shows packets that never existed in that size on the network. This is a capture-point artefact, not a fault. Large frames do not mean jumbo frames are in use.

title: Duplicate frames from the capture setup
summary: 2 'retransmissions' carry the same IP identification number as the original frame, so they are the same packet captured twice (typical of a SPAN/mirror port that copies both ingress and egress, or capturing on two interfaces). They have been excluded from the packet-loss figures.

title: The capture missed packets (capture drops)
summary: 2 ACKs on 1 connection(s) acknowledge data that never appears in the capture (2 gaps seen). The receiver got the data, so the network delivered it; the capturing machine failed to record it (busy CPU, small capture buffer, or a mirror port that was oversubscribed). Gaps alone are not proof of network loss.
